coverage_limits: osv-scanner still detects ZERO npm packages and no node binary in the vidra-user image (18 Alpine packages only). The frontend answer in this record comes from npm audit on the lockfile plus reading the shipped /app/node_modules/*/package.json, not from the image scan.

govulncheck alone would still miss GHSA-only Go advisories (the v0.6.4 grpc finding, T4, was invisible to it); osv-scanner on the binary is what covers that class, and Dependabot alerts are a third, independent opinion.
Binary-mode govulncheck cannot prove reachability. The x/crypto rows are answered with the linux/amd64 package graph instead.

No reproducible-build check was attempted: this record does NOT prove the published binaries were built from the scanned source. It proves the images carry org.opencontainers.image.revision equal to the scanned commits, which is an assertion by the builder, plus a provenance attestation manifest that nothing in deploy tooling verifies.
This is artifact evidence only. Nothing here says anything about runtime acceptance of v0.6.5.
vidra-core's Python tree was not separately lock-scanned: the image carries exactly one PyPI package record and no uv/pip lockfile is committed for the runtime image.
exact_candidate_security_facet: PASS for v0.6.5 as published, with two named residuals that have no upstream fix (x/crypto GO-2026-5932, not linked into either binary; the rav1e/libdovi Rust crate advisories, no Alpine v3.24 fix) and one scanner false positive (glib). Every advisory with a released fix that the v0.6.4 record found in shipped artifacts - next 16.3.0, Alpine openssl 3.5.7-r0, grpc 1.83.1 - is gone from the v0.6.5 artifacts, verified in the artifact itself and not only in a lockfile. This facet does not promote any runtime workflow row.
